issues.description: Behavior change: coerceNumber now silently maps non-numerics to 0 instead of propagating null
issues.detail: The old panLinear/zoomLinear passed toNumber as lift; a non-numeric domain entry would produce NaN downstream (visible nonsense). The new coerceNumber substitutes 0 on null, which silently distorts the domain instead of failing loudly. That is a real semantic change hidden inside a 'just added types' PR. Either preserve NaN propagation or document the new contract.

issues.description: Domain type is the wrong data structure; signatures still take number[] then runtime-check non-empty
issues.detail: Pike's rule: data dominates. The right type is NonEmptyArray<number> (or readonly [number, number]) at the public boundary, so callers cannot pass []. Instead the API accepts number[] and throws at runtime, which is exactly what types were supposed to eliminate. Push the constraint into the signature and the isNonEmpty guard disappears.

issues.description: identity was deleted from accessors import but a local one-line identity was reintroduced
issues.detail: The original code reused identity from ./accessors.js. The new file inlines a typed identity and adds a typed coerceNumber wrapper. Fine, but the comment says these adapt to TransformFn; the simpler move is to fix the type of the shared identity/toNumber once and keep one definition. Small duplication, but it is duplication.

issues.description: Only panLinear/zoomLinear empty-domain throws are tested; the other six entry points are not
issues.detail: The runtime guard lives in pan() and zoom(), so it does cover all callers, but the test suite only exercises two. A one-line table-driven test over all eight entry points would prove the contract cheaply and document the new behavior. n is small; the test should be small too.

issues.description: peek overload pair is correct but slightly more machinery than the data shape needs
issues.detail: Two overloads plus an implementation signature for a one-line array[length-1]. If the callers used NonEmptyArray at the boundary (see above), peek would not need an overload at all; the single typed signature would suffice. Worth keeping if other callers rely on the undefined branch, otherwise it is framework where a struct would do.

review.summary: The refactor is small, composable, and mostly earns its keep — types added without churning the algorithms, which is the right move. Two concerns: the data structure is still wrong at the boundary (number[] plus runtime check, instead of NonEmptyArray in the signature), and coerceNumber silently substitutes 0 for null where the old code would propagate NaN — a quiet semantic change inside a 'just types' PR. Fix the type at the edge and the isNonEmpty guard, the throw, and the extra tests all collapse into the signature. Tone otherwise: small, clear, and the right shape.
